question.text: A Pre-emptive Right entitles an existing shareholder to:

answer.text: Maintain their percentage shareholding by participating pro-rata in future rounds of financing or stock option exercises
Receive dividends before common shareholders only
Vote with 2x voting power on all ordinary resolutions
Block the company from issuing any new debt securities

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Series XIX-C page 292, a pre-emptive right lets an existing shareholder maintain their percentage shareholding through the right to participate and purchase pro-rata in shares issued in future financing rounds or stock options exercised. It is a right, not an obligation. The Trap: Pre-emptive rights concern shareholding percentage, not dividend priority, voting multipliers, or vetoes over debt issuance — those describe other categories of preferential or restrictive rights. Note: Anchor the answer on the page 292 pre-emptive-right definition.
